We need to find the score minus penalties. Starting at index 0, we will have accumulated point: dp[0] = nums[0]

Transition:

For each position i from 1 to n-1, you can come from any previous j < i.

dp[i] = nums[i] + max{ dp[j] - (x if parity different else 0) } 

This is O(n^2), too big. We need linear.

Observation: The penalty depends only on parity difference. So we can maintain the best total score seen so far for each parity (even/odd), subtract x if moving from opposite parity.

We can compute:

Let best_even = max total score ending at a position with even nums[j] (including that nums[j] value)
Let best_odd = max total score ending at a position with odd nums[j]

Initialize:

if nums[0] even: best_even = nums[0]; best_odd = -inf
else: best_odd = nums[0]; best_even = -inf

For i from 1 to n-1:
    parity = nums[i] % 2
    if parity == 0: # even
        # from same parity: best_even (no penalty)
        # from opposite: best_odd - x (penalty)
        cand = max(best_even, best_odd - x)
        dp_i = nums[i] + cand
        best_even = max(best_even, dp_i)
    else:
        cand = max(best_odd, best_even - x)
        dp_i = nums[i] + cand
        best_odd = max(best_odd, dp_i)

Answer = max(best_even, best_odd)

But note dp_i could be less than previous best_even? We update best_even with max.

Works.

Edge case: what if no path? We always can stay at start? Actually we must start at index 0; we can choose not to move? Score will be nums[0]? Yes.

Our DP considers any path ending at i. At the end, answer is max over all i.
